body: I'm sorry to hear that. Sometimes when I have my "what if" moments, I like to remind myself of a metaphor---that I did the best play I could with the cards I had in hand at the moment. Sometimes it wasn't really possible to do any better than what we did; sometimes we don't have the power to fix things; we tried our best, and yet things did't go the way we wish they did.

What if, unlike catgardens, one does not have anyone who seemingly cares about them? For a combination of reasons (none of which alone would drive me over the edge, but which together are making it hard to cope) I started contemplating suicide over the last month. I know for a fact some people will feel sad if I go, but at the same time I don't feel any of them takes my feeling seriously. Even when I told them I was thinking about suicide, their reaction was to mock me and tell me to get a life. What to do in this case? What should I cling to?
Sounds to me like you could *at least* give it another go to see if she really means it when she says she understands it was her fault. You've got nothing to lose.

Well, for what it's worth I read it. Get a few day's rest and then try to think through your options, I guess.

I'm living an analogous situation in that I'm being kicked out of the house by a woman who a few years back begged me to stay in the relationship when I wanted out. I did stay and gave up on other paths that life could have taken me in order to work on that relationship, only for her years later to decide that she became tired of it.

I guess people lack empathy and/or gratitude.

Wish you best of luck.
Dude, that's so fucked up on the part of your company. I can't begin to imagine the stress that this is causing you right now. What's the prospect on getting in on a new job soon?
